632:
This article is not intended to repeal or modify in any way any other ordinance of the county relating to the abatement of or punishment for nuisances, junk or other matters affecting the health and safety of the public. All remedies provided in this article are supplemental to and in addition to all other remedies provided by the codes and ordinances of the county and by state laws.
(Ord. of 5-14-96, § IX; Ord. of 9-18-07; Ord. of 9-20-22, § 1)
635:
The following practices and procedures shall be followed by persons in the unincorporated areas of the county in order to facilitate the collection of solid waste:
(1) Refuse. All refuse shall be managed by such persons in accordance with applicable laws, and all municipal solid waste shall be placed and maintained in containers satisfying the requirements of this article and of the rules and regulations of the CA. Containers shall be maintained at all times with tightfitting lids or covers, and secured in such manner as to prevent the overturning by the elements or by dogs or other animals. All refuse to be collected by the county's contractor shall be placed in containers provided by the county or the county contractor or designee.
(2) Garbage. Garbage placed in containers for collection shall be enclosed in paper or plastic bags. Garbage shall be drained of all liquids prior to placement in refuse receptacles.
(3) Injurious trash items. Municipal solid waste or refuse brought to the county transfer station with potential for inflicting injury, such as broken glass, light bulbs, sharp pieces of metal, fluorescent tubes, and television tubes shall be securely packaged or wrapped in such a manner as will prevent injury to the collection crews or other persons. The provisions of this subsection shall not apply to material placed in mechanically handled containers.
(4) Hazardous waste. Hazardous waste will not be collected by the county or county contractor. No person shall place any hazardous waste in any refuse receptacle or other container for collection and shall not haul or deliver any hazardous waste to the county transfer station. All applicable laws relating to the generation, management, handling, treatment, storage or disposal of hazardous waste shall be observed by all persons, and the county reserves the right to report any discovered or known violations of such laws to the appropriate state, federal or local authorities.
(5) Building materials and construction debris. Building materials and construction debris will not be collected by the county. The owner of the premises or the contractor, builder or person doing the repairs, remodeling construction or demolition shall be required to haul and transfer the debris to the county transfer station or other waste disposal site.
(6) Tree and vegetable removal; home occupants. Trees cut by the owner or occupant shall be taken to the transfer station by the owner or other waste disposal site. When a tree is cut from private property by anyone other than the owner, such party shall remove and legally dispose of all wood and limbs. The owner, tenant or other persons in possession of the property shall be responsible to see that such tree trimmer or other person outlined above complies with this provision.
(7) Other yard debris. Grass clippings, leaves, pine straw and/or pine cones shall only be placed for collection at the shoulder of the road if the homeowner has arranged for the pickup of yard debris by the county's contractor at the homeowner's expense. Any yard debris to be collected shall be prepared for collection in accordance with the contractor's instructions. Failure to arrange for collection and failure to comply with the contractor's instructions shall be a violation of this ordinance.
(8) Ashes. It shall be unlawful to deposit hot ashes in garbage containers. Ashes or clinkers shall not be placed or deposited upon streets, sidewalks or side parks.
(9) Pet litter. Pet litter must be placed in securely tied plastic bags not to exceed ten pounds in weight and placed in the container.
(10) Household furniture, furnishings, and appliances. The county or county contractor will collect large appliances, tables, couches, chairs, and other forms of brown and white goods generated from single and multi-family residential dwelling units provided the residents contact the county or county contractor in advance to make arrangements for a large item pick up in accordance with the provisions of the county's solid waste contract. All brown and white goods must be disposed of as instructed by the county or contractor. Failure to comply with the county's or contractor's instructions shall be considered a violation of this article.
(11) Disposable diapers. Disposable diapers must be placed and tied securely in plastic bags and placed in the regular container.
(12) Rock, dirt, and similar materials. The county or county contractor shall not be responsible for collection of discarded dirt, rock or any other natural materials.
(13) Tires. The owner or occupant of any premises shall be responsible for the sanitary handling and lawful disposing of all scrap tires on the premises used or occupied by such person.
(14) Industrial and animal waste. Industrial waste, any and all dead animals, or waste from construction, demolition, landscaping or processing operations will not be collected, transported or disposed of by the county or county contractor. The collection, transportation and disposal of such waste shall be the responsibility of the owners and/or generators of such waste or animals.
(Ord. of 5-14-96, § III; Ord. of 11-13-18(3), § 1; Ord. of 9-20-22, § 1)
636:
(a) Residential. Garbage accumulated by residents shall be stored in refuse containers provided by the county or county contractor and shall be placed at such locations convenient for servicing by the county as designated by the CA or designee for weekly pickup. Service for disabled citizens will be handled through appropriate accommodations arranged through the CA or designee.
(b) Commercial. Refuse accumulated by commercial establishments shall be stored in containers meeting the requirements of the CA as to size, shape and materials; and such receptacles shall be compatible with the collection equipment and methods of the county or county contractor.
(c) Issuance of permits. The building inspector of the county shall not issue a building permit for industrial establishments, commercial establishments or multi-family dwellings until the CA gives his approval to proposed plans for the storage, disposal and other management of refuse, and until the applicant for a permit has submitted proof that all the applicant's taxes and fees due the county are paid and are current. The term, "applicant's taxes and fees" includes any and all taxes and fees on property that the applicant has an interest in or is responsible for managing.
(d) Locations of containers. The county or county contractor will not collect municipal solid waste from commercial establishments or multi-family dwellings unless the municipal solid waste is placed in approved containers and located at a place approved by the CA.
(e) Multi-family units. All multi-family dwellings served by the county or county contractor shall be containerized with plastic or metal containers furnished by the county or county contractor. Each multi-family dwelling shall utilize the type and number of containers assigned by the CA or designee in accordance with sections 54-58 and 54-60.
(f) Containerizing trash. All commercial establishments shall containerize all refuse generated by the establishment, including outside as well as inside debris from the premises.
(g) Transfer station. All industrial waste, building material, roofing material, material from remodeling and demolition that is hauled and taken to the transfer station in accordance with this article shall be hauled and taken by the owner or by the person responsible to the owner for the removal of such material in compliance with applicable laws.
(Ord. of 5-14-96, § IV; Ord. of 11-13-18(3), § 1; Ord. of 9-20-22, § 1)
637:
(a) Inspections. Where a wheeled garbage container is furnished by the county, it shall be the only container authorized for garbage collection and shall be subject to inspection by the county. Should additional containers be needed, they may be obtained for a fee by contacting the CA.
(b) Placing for collection. The owner, occupant, tenant, or other person occupying any building, house or structure within the unincorporated areas of the county as a residence or business using a wheeled garbage container shall have the container at the curb or designated location not earlier than 7:00 p.m. on the day before and not later than 7:00 a.m. on the designated garbage pickup days.
(c) Removal after collection. The owners, occupant, tenant, or other person occupying any building, house or structure within the unincorporated areas of the county as a residence or business using a wheeled garbage container for curb side service shall return the container to the side or rear of building no later than 24 hours after collection. Where the collection point is located more than 100 yards from a home, the container may be stored at another location approved by the CA.
(d) Vacating dwelling. Wheeled garbage containers furnished by the county shall not be removed from the premises to which they are delivered.
(e) Loss or damage to container. If the wheeled container furnished by the county is damaged, lost, or destroyed through negligence of the person to whom the container was assigned, the person shall reimburse the county for the cost of a replacement container.
(Ord. of 5-14-96, § V; Ord. of 11-13-18(3), § 1; Ord. of 9-20-22, § 1)
638:
(a) Generally. Commercial establishments shall store refuse in containers meeting the requirements of applicable laws, including but not limited to this article and the rules and regulations promulgated by the CA in part to eliminate wind-driven debris and unsightly litter in and about the establishment. Any spillage or overflow shall be cleaned up immediately by the establishment.
(b) Loading and unloading areas. All loading and unloading areas shall be provided with appropriate refuse receptacles for loose debris, paper, packaging materials and other trash and refuse. The owner or occupant of the commercial establishment shall place a sufficient number of containers, not less than the number required by the rules and regulations adopted by the board of commissioners for that establishment, in the area to maintain a clean, neat and sanitary condition at all times. The occupant of the premises shall maintain surveillance to ensure that all refuse is placed in the proper container in compliance with applicable laws, including but not limited to this article, and that the area is kept clean and free of litter.
(Ord. of 5-14-96, § VI; Ord. of 11-13-18(3), § 1)

645:

647:

(1) Throw or deposit any refuse on any public or private street or scatter such refuse or litter on any public or private property.

648:
(a) No vehicle shall be driven or moved on any public road in the unincorporated areas of the county unless such vehicle is constructed or loaded or covered in such a manner so as to prevent any of its load from blowing out, dropping, escaping, or shifting in such a manner as to:
(1) Create a safety hazard; or
(2) Deposit litter, rubbish, junk, trash or debris on public or private property.
Nothing in this section shall prohibit the necessary spreading of any substance in public road maintenance.
(b) No person shall load any vehicle, which is to be operated on any public road in the unincorporated areas of this county, unless such load is fully covered and the covering thereon is securely fastened so as to prevent said covering or load from:
(1) Becoming loose, detached, or in any manner becoming a hazard to other users of the public road; or
(2) Depositing litter, rubbish, junk, trash or debris on public or private property while such vehicle is on a public road.
(c) Nothing in this section shall be deemed to supersede any federal or state laws or regulations applying to the securing of loads on motor vehicles.
(d) The provisions of this section and regulations based thereon shall not apply to organic debris that escapes during the transportation of silage from field or farm to storage and storage to feedlot or during the transportation of agricultural or farm products or silvicultural products from farm or forest to a processing plant or point of sale or use.
